marker: # unit_length is the Average repeat size of Table 1, except at VNTR63_01, and it is an average
# because these arrays are imperfect: the same table counts the variable bases per locus, from
# none at VNTR67_01 and VNTR21_01 to 23 of 66 at VNTR61_02 and 26 of 81 at VNTR81_01.
# The unit lengths were checked by amplifying all eight loci in eight S. aureus genomes, N315,
# Mu50, MW2, COL, MRSA252, MSSA476, NCTC 8325 and USA300. The flanking length of a locus does not
# change between strains, so every product of that locus must leave the same remainder when
# divided by the repeat unit. That test gives:
#   VNTR09_01  consistent at 9 bp, five distinct sizes from 319 to 409
#   VNTR21_01  consistent at 21 bp for seven of the eight; MRSA252 is one base shorter than the
#              others, an indel in the flank rather than a repeat difference
#   VNTR24_01  consistent at 24 bp
#   VNTR81_01  consistent at 81 bp
#   VNTR63_01  NOT consistent at the published 64 bp and exactly consistent at 63 bp, every size
#              differing by a multiple of 63, so 63 is recorded here and 64 is the average the
#              paper prints
#   VNTR67_01  no single period fits: the observed sizes step by 67 and by 133, so units of 67 and
#              66 alternate and the published 67 is the average of the two
#   VNTR61_02  no period fits; this is the locus with 23 variable bases in a 66 bp unit
#   VNTR61_01  no period fits, which is the behaviour the paper itself reports for this locus,
#              that its upstream flanking region is heterogeneous and gives slightly larger and
#              smaller fragments, so the bins had to be shifted by hand to the observed sizes
# ref_size is the product these primers give in the N315 assembly GCA_000009645.1. Every locus
# gives exactly one product with no primer mismatch, and all eight lengths equal the span of the
# coordinates Table 2 gives in NC_002745 for the same primer pair, which is an exact independent
# check of both the primers and the coordinates.
# ref_repeats IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY, SO THIS SCHEME SIZES ITS MARKERS WITHOUT CALLING THEM.
# The paper derives an allele as the product length minus the flanking length, divided by the
# repeat size, but it publishes neither the flanking length nor the repeat unit sequences, and it
# does not state the repeat number of the sequenced reference. The eight genome comparison above
# fixes each flanking length only up to a whole number of repeats, because every candidate flank
# that differs by one unit explains all eight strains equally well, and the repeat ranges Table 1
# reports narrow that to about ten candidates per locus rather than to one. Locating the arrays in
# N315 directly does not settle it either: the repeats are imperfect enough that the boundary of
# the best periodic region is uncertain by a fraction of a unit, and at VNTR81_01 the whole
# amplicon scores as periodic, which would leave less flank than the two primers occupy. A wrong
# reference count shifts every allele at that locus by a constant and would be invisible in the
# output, so no count is recorded rather than a doubtful one.
# To enable calling, supply either the flanking lengths, which fix ref_repeats for the measured
# sizes above, or the published size to allele table as bins.tsv. Table 1 bounds what to expect:
# the repeat range over the 1681 isolates is 6-25 for VNTR09_01, 0-6 VNTR61_01, 0-5 VNTR61_02,
# FOUR LOCI ARE ANCHORED TO PUBLISHED REFERENCE COUNTS. The Pourcel et al. 14 locus S. aureus panel,
# bundled here as saureus_mlva14_pourcel_2009 with its reference counts from Pourcel et al. 2009 and
# Bogut et al. 2024 (doi:10.2478/cipms-2024-0014), contains four VNTRs that are the same physical
# arrays this panel reads under different primers. They are identified by the Pourcel locus name,
# which encodes the genomic position in kb, together with the repeat unit, each confirmed to sit at
# the same Mu50 position as this panel's amplicon with the same unit length:
#   VNTR24_01 = Sa0122, 122 kb, 24 bp (the spa repeat), Mu50 count 10
#   VNTR63_01 = Sa1132, 1132 kb, 63 bp, Mu50 count 6
#   VNTR67_01 = Sa0704, 704 kb, 67 bp, Mu50 count 4
#   VNTR81_01 = Sa0266, 266 kb, 81 bp (the coa repeat), Mu50 count 6
# The array is the same DNA whichever primers flank it, so its repeat count is the same for both
# schemes. This panel's amplicon in Mu50 equals its amplicon in N315, the reference here, at all
# four loci, so the Mu50 count transfers unchanged to ref_repeats, and a run on N315 returns it with
# zero residual. The Pourcel Mu50 counts at Sa0122 and Sa1132 are further confirmed across the 31
# isolates of Bogut et al. Table 3, where each leaves a constant flank.
# VNTR67_01 is anchored for the reference but its array is not a clean single period in every
# lineage: across eight sequenced genomes N315, Mu50 and MRSA252 give a whole allele while MW2,
# MSSA476, COL, NCTC8325 and USA300 give a fractional one, because the array there mixes 67 bp and
# 66 bp units. Those strains are reported INTERMEDIATE rather than rounded, which is the honest
# signal that a single unit model does not fit them; the reference call is unaffected. VNTR81_01 is
# the coa array, and this panel's primers lie inside it, so the flank is only about 10 bp; the allele
# formula needs only ref_size and ref_repeats, which are consistent, and all eight genomes give a
# whole allele, though coa also carries a half-repeat polymorphism that can give an n.5 allele in
# other strains.
# The anchor does not reach the other four loci, VNTR09_01, VNTR61_01, VNTR61_02 and VNTR21_01, which
# are not in the Pourcel 14 panel, so they stay sized only. The absolute scale of the four filled
# loci is the Pourcel convention, which may differ from Schouls' own published allele numbers by a
# constant per locus.
